title: Fin alternatives for B2B support teams in 2026
summary: Compare 7 Fin alternatives for B2B support, including Pylon, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Help Scout, Front, HubSpot, and Plain. Pricing and fit.
body_markdown:
Fin is a strong AI agent for automated resolution, especially on questions a knowledge base can answer. B2B teams start looking at Fin alternatives when support is account-based, customers ask in Slack Connect and Microsoft Teams, and every issue needs investigation across product and CRM systems, not only a resolved chat.


Quick note on names: the company formerly called Intercom renamed itself Fin in May 2026. The help desk product is still called Intercom. Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin on September 10, 2026; Fin operates within Salesforce AI Labs. Below, we use **Intercom** for the help desk and **Fin** for the agent. For a direct side-by-side, see[Pylon vs Fin](https://www.usepylon.com/competitors/fin) .


Loop moved from Intercom to Pylon. Owen Murk, Product Support Specialist at Loop, said: "Our responsibilities differ a lot across people and accounts. Intercom worked for agents who just answer a ticket and move to the next one, but that was a really small percentage of the support we were doing." After the move, Loop reported average resolution time down 20%, and about 25% of customers supported via Slack, a channel unlocked on Pylon.


This guide covers 7 Fin alternatives, where each fits, and what each costs to start.


## Why B2B teams look for a Fin alternative


Fin bills per outcome (from $0.99 per outcome on fin.ai and Intercom pricing). It can run on the Intercom help desk or on another help desk. That model fits high-volume resolution on repeatable questions.


B2B support often needs more than resolution count:


- Shared Slack and Microsoft Teams channels treated as first-class support work.
- Account context (ARR, stakeholders, open issues, health) in every investigation.
- Agents that start work before a human opens the issue.
- Seat-plus-credits pricing that does not grow only with resolved conversations.


## What to look for in a Fin alternative


- Native Slack Connect and Microsoft Teams as customer channels.
- Agents that investigate across CRM, issue trackers, product data, and past conversations.
- Skills or procedures humans and agents both run.
- Clear pricing: seats, credits, or per-resolution, stated up front.
- A migration path for conversations, customers, knowledge, and workflows.


## The 7 best Fin alternatives


### Pylon


**Best for:** B2B teams that support customers in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, and chat, and need agents that investigate with account context.


Pylon is the agentic support platform built for B2B. Slack Connect, Slack Community, email, the chat widget, Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, and ticket forms are on every plan. Microsoft Teams and Google Chat are on Advanced and Enterprise. Conversations become issues in one inbox, linked to the account.


Where Fin focuses on customer-facing resolution (and Copilot as an inbox assistant add-on), Pylon's Automations can start when an issue arrives: gather account context, check connected systems, and run Skills before someone opens it. Agents investigate issues before your team opens them, so your team starts with evidence and recommended next steps.


- Support Agent answers from your content, collects information, gathers internal context, and can resolve issues end to end.
- Assist Agent investigates issues, drafts replies, and takes actions using workspace context.
- Slack Agent lets teammates you give access to ask about a customer or take approved actions from Slack.
- Automations run on an event or schedule.
- Skills are reusable instructions that people and agents both run. Skills are on every plan and don't use credits.


Nexus is Pylon's versioned agent harness: context, memory, traces, routing, guardrails, and improve, over Support, Account, and Product Intelligence layers.


Proof from customers who left Intercom: Loop's Owen Murk also said, "My team now comes to me asking, 'Can we do this in Pylon?' The answer is usually yes, and quickly. That just wasn't the case in Intercom." Pylon's own support team adopted Agentic Support and cut median first-response time 72%, from 19.4 to 5.3 minutes.


**Pricing:** Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month, on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features run on credits, with a 5,000 credit minimum commitment. Pylon doesn't charge per issue. See[Pylon pricing](https://www.usepylon.com/pricing) . Trusted by 1,800+ B2B customers globally.


**Tradeoffs:** no free plan, a minimum seat count for new customers, and Microsoft Teams needs Advanced. If your main need is per-outcome deflection on Intercom or another help desk, Fin remains a strong fit.


Migrating from Intercom / Fin: The[Intercom migration guide](https://support.usepylon.com/articles/1404041524-migrating-from-intercom) covers companies, contacts, conversations, teams, tickets, and knowledge base content. Migrated tickets arrive closed. Across 300+ migrations from Zendesk, Intercom, and Salesforce, 90% finished in under 2 months. See[Pylon vs Fin](https://www.usepylon.com/competitors/fin) .


### Zendesk


**Best for:** large teams that want deep configuration and a big app ecosystem.


Zendesk's Suite plans bring email, messaging, phone, and social together. Plans include AI agents with automated resolutions per agent, then additional resolutions billed. Copilot is an add-on on Professional and higher. Support Team starts at $19 per agent per month paid yearly. See[Pylon vs Zendesk](https://www.usepylon.com/competitors/zendesk) .


### Freshdesk


**Best for:** teams that want classic ticketing at a low entry price.


Freshdesk includes ticketing, a shared inbox, a customer portal, and a knowledge base on every paid plan. Freddy AI Agent includes 500 free sessions once per account. Growth is $19 per agent per month billed annually. Freddy AI Copilot is a per-agent add-on on Pro and Enterprise.


### Help Scout


**Best for:** small teams that want a simpler shared inbox.


Help Scout covers email, live chat, SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger on paid plans, with a free plan for up to 5 users. Envoy (AI Answers) is billed per resolution. Standard is $25 per user per month.


### Front


**Best for:** email-first teams that want a collaborative inbox.


Front's Starter plan is $25 per seat per month billed annually. Copilot is a per-seat add-on on Starter and Professional (included in Enterprise). Autopilot is billed per conversation. See[Pylon vs Front](https://www.usepylon.com/competitors/front) .


### HubSpot Service Hub


**Best for:** teams that run sales and marketing on HubSpot.


Service Hub connects chat, email, forms, calling, WhatsApp, and Facebook Messenger next to CRM records. Customer Agent runs on HubSpot Credits. HubSpot Service Hub has a free edition, with paid seats from $20 per seat per month, billed monthly. You can keep HubSpot CRM while moving support elsewhere (Pylon syncs with HubSpot).


### Plain


**Best for:** technical B2B teams that support customers in Slack.


Plain's Foundation plan includes Slack, email, and in-app channels and AI agents on monthly credits at $45 per user per month billed annually. Microsoft Teams is on Horizon. See[Pylon vs Plain](https://www.usepylon.com/competitors/plain) .

## Which Fin alternative is right for you?


Stay with Fin if most work is automated resolution on chat and email and per-outcome pricing fits your volume. Pick Zendesk or Freshdesk for classic enterprise or low-entry ticketing, Help Scout for a simpler inbox, Front for collaborative email, HubSpot Service Hub if your CRM is HubSpot, and Pylon if customers live in Slack and Teams and every issue needs account-aware investigation.[Book a demo](https://www.usepylon.com/get-started) .

### What is the best Fin alternative for B2B support?


For B2B teams that support customers in Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email and need account context in every issue, Pylon is built for that. Zendesk suits large teams that want deep configuration, and Plain suits technical teams centered on Slack.


### Is Fin the same as Intercom?


The company formerly called Intercom renamed itself Fin in May 2026. The help desk product is still called Intercom. Fin is the AI agent. Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin on September 10, 2026.


### How is Pylon priced compared with Fin?


Pylon Professional is $89 per seat per month and Advanced is $139 per seat per month, on an annual contract. Enterprise is a custom quote. Agentic features run on credits, and Pylon doesn't charge per issue. Fin is from $0.99 per outcome, on Intercom or on another help desk (with a monthly outcome minimum when Fin runs alone).


### How long does it take to migrate from Intercom to Pylon?


It depends on your channels, integrations, and history. Across 300+ migrations from Zendesk, Intercom, and Salesforce, 90% finished in under 2 months.


### Has anyone moved from Intercom to Pylon?


Yes. Loop migrated from Intercom to Pylon and reported average resolution time down 20%, with about 25% of customers supported via Slack after the move.
